material_systems.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer for Traditional Stucco

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec Masonry & Stucco Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY on ALL new traditional stucco regardless of quality tier — pH up to 13 requires alkali-resistant primer. Standard acrylic primer is NOT suitable. SW Loxon enables 7-day accelerated coating (vs 28-day standard cure). Coverage varies by texture: smooth stucco 300-350 SF/gal, sand 225-275 SF/gal, lace/dash significantly lower — apply texture multiplier from coverage profile.

material_systems.notes: Non-negotiable primer for new traditional stucco. Alkali-resistance is not quality-optional — even QT2 economy must use this primer. Oil-based/alkyd PROHIBITED (saponification). Coverage is texture-dependent; base rate assumes smooth stucco with texture multiplier applied separately.

material_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Exterior Primer for EIFS

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Exterior Primer
primer.notes: Standard 100% acrylic primer for EIFS substrate. EIFS is NOT alkaline — alkali-resistant primer is not required. EIFS surface is smoother and less porous than traditional stucco, resulting in higher coverage rates. Must be vapor permeable to allow moisture vapor transmission through the EIFS system.

material_systems.notes: EIFS primer selection is chemistry-driven, not pH-driven. The key requirement is vapor permeability and flexibility — EIFS moves thermally and the primer must accommodate without cracking. Oil-based/alkyd PROHIBITED (incompatible with EIFS system).

material_systems.name: Standard 100% Acrylic Exterior Finish for Stucco

finish.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior for both traditional stucco and EIFS wall field. Vapor permeable (10-20 perms) — preserves moisture vapor transmission critical for both substrate types. Coverage is base rate on smooth stucco — apply texture multiplier for sand/lace/dash profiles. QT2 allows single finish coat on properly primed surface. QT3 requires two coats standard. DFT is total (2 coats at QT3).

material_systems.notes: Primary finish system for residential stucco at standard and economy tiers. Flat is budget standard — hides texture irregularities. Satin provides durability and cleanability. Semi-gloss NOT recommended for stucco wall field — texture irregularities are magnified. Coverage is lower than smooth siding due to stucco porosity and texture.

material_systems.name: Premium 100% Acrylic Exterior Finish for Stucco

finish.notes: Premium 100% acrylic for QT4 stucco. Superior color retention, fade resistance, UV stability, and washability. Raking light inspection between coats on visible areas. Texture-matching patch verification required. DFT is total (2 coats). Coverage base rate on smooth — apply texture multiplier.

material_systems.notes: Premium tier for high-end residential stucco. Same sheen options as standard — semi-gloss is not appropriate for textured stucco wall field. Premium products provide better hide, superior color retention, and extended durability (15-20 year expected life vs 10-12 for standard).

material_systems.name: Elastomeric Coating for Traditional Stucco

hard_blockers.message: Elastomeric coatings are STRICTLY PROHIBITED on EIFS. Elastomeric on EIFS traps moisture behind the EPS insulation board, causing mold growth, substrate deterioration, and catastrophic system delamination. This is a non-negotiable hard blocker — no exceptions.

products: Benjamin Moore Super Spec Elastomeric Waterproof Coating
finish.notes: Elastomeric coating for traditional stucco ONLY: 12-20 mils DFT total (2 coats mandatory), >300% elongation bridges hairline cracks up to 1/16 inch. Two coats mandatory — single coat cannot achieve required DFT. Coverage is dramatically lower than standard acrylic due to thick-film DFT requirement. Requires 527-535 spray tip and 30-mesh filter for airless application. Material cost is 3-4x that of standard acrylic; combined with lower coverage, material cost per SF is 5-8x higher. Requires documented moisture source assessment before specification.

material_systems.notes: Elastomeric coatings are inherently flat/low-sheen due to extreme film thickness. NOT available at QT2 — application complexity exceeds economy scope. WARNING: High risk of catastrophic delamination if moisture enters from alternate sources (ground water, plumbing leaks, rising damp). Requires documented moisture source assessment. NEVER ON EIFS — this is the single most critical material routing rule in this spec family.

smooth.notes: Smooth stucco (trowel finish) — lowest porosity of traditional stucco textures. Best primer coverage.

sand.notes: Sand finish — moderate texture depth, moderate porosity. Common residential stucco texture.

lace.notes: Lace (Spanish lace) — deeper texture recesses consume more primer. Coverage drops significantly.

dash.notes: Dash/roughcast — deepest texture profile. Highest material consumption. Coverage is comparable to CMU block filler.

assumptions: Coverage rates are for spray_backroll application (primary method for stucco field).
Spray_backroll transfer efficiency already accounted for in range — approximately 65-75% on stucco.
Texture modifier is derived from coverage ratio: smooth 325 SF/gal baseline. Modifier = baseline / texture rate.
Roll-only application achieves similar coverage per gallon but lower production rate.

EIFS.notes: EIFS surface is factory-applied acrylic finish — smoother and less porous than any traditional stucco texture. Consistent coverage. Texture modifier not applicable to EIFS.

assumptions: EIFS has a single texture profile — the factory-applied acrylic finish coat. No texture modifier required.
Coverage is significantly higher than traditional stucco primer due to sealed, non-porous substrate.
Spray_backroll or roll application. Spray-only prohibited per doctrine.

smooth.notes: Smooth stucco on primed surface. Primer seals some porosity — finish coat coverage is near the upper range.

sand.notes: Sand finish on primed surface. Moderate texture still consumes additional material despite priming.

lace.notes: Lace texture on primed surface. Deep recesses require more material per SF even on primed substrate.

dash.notes: Dash/roughcast on primed surface. Highest material consumption for acrylic finish — deep texture profile dominates.

EIFS.notes: EIFS on primed surface — smoothest substrate in the stucco family. Highest finish coat coverage.

assumptions: Coverage per coat. Two-coat system at QT3/QT4 doubles material consumption.
Spray_backroll application: transfer efficiency factored into range.
Premium acrylic (QT4) has comparable coverage to standard — higher solids offset by better hide.
EIFS coverage is higher than smooth traditional stucco due to non-porous sealed surface.

smooth.notes: Elastomeric on smooth traditional stucco. Dramatically lower coverage than acrylic due to 12-20 mil DFT target. 3-4x material consumption vs acrylic.

sand.notes: Elastomeric on sand texture. Texture recesses require heavy-body fill, further reducing coverage.

lace.notes: Elastomeric on lace texture. Deep texture profile combined with thick-film DFT requirement creates very high material consumption.

dash.notes: Elastomeric on dash/roughcast. Maximum material consumption — deepest texture plus thickest DFT. A 1000 SF dash wall may consume 30-35 gallons of elastomeric per coat.

assumptions: Coverage per coat. Two coats mandatory — single coat cannot achieve 12-20 mil DFT target.
Spray_backroll is the ONLY practical method for elastomeric at production scale (too thick for roller-only on large areas).
Transfer efficiency for elastomeric spray is lower than acrylic (~50-60%) due to heavy-body material — already factored into range.
Material cost: elastomeric is approximately $50-80/gal vs $30-45/gal for standard acrylic. Combined with 2-3x lower coverage, material cost per SF is 5-8x higher.
EIFS is intentionally excluded — elastomeric on EIFS is a HARD BLOCKER.

consumables.name: Roller cover 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap (stucco texture)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 150 SF rolled (heavy stucco texture shreds nap faster than smooth surfaces)
consumables.notes: Heavy nap roller for porous/textured stucco surfaces. Nylon/polyester blend for water-based acrylic and elastomeric products. Required for backroll step in spray_backroll and for roll-only applications. Nap selection: smooth stucco 3/4-1 inch, sand 1-1/4 inch, lace/dash 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch.

consumables.name: Roller cover 3/4 inch nap (EIFS smooth surface)
consumables.notes: Medium nap roller for EIFS surfaces. EIFS has a smooth acrylic finish — heavy nap is unnecessary and creates stipple that may not match the factory texture. 3/4 inch nap provides adequate material deposit without excessive texture.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 517/619 (stucco acrylic/primer)
consumables.notes: 0.017 orifice (517) for standard acrylic latex and alkali-resistant primer on stucco. Also 619, 621 for wider patterns on large wall fields. Cementitious stucco causes faster tip wear than wood substrates — shorter service life per tip.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 527-535 (elastomeric coating)
consumables.notes: 0.027-0.035 orifice (527, 531, 535 range) for heavy-body elastomeric coatings. Requires 2,300-3,000 PSI. Faster wear rate due to thick-body material and abrasive cementitious substrate. Budget for 50% more tips per gallon than acrylic spray.

consumables.name: 60-mesh spray filter (black) for acrylic latex
consumables.notes: Standard 60-mesh (black/medium) filter for acrylic latex exterior coatings and alkali-resistant primer. Change when flow rate drops. Not suitable for elastomeric — use 30-mesh.

consumables.name: 30-mesh spray filter (gray/coarse) for elastomeric
consumables.notes: Coarse 30-mesh (gray) filter for elastomeric coatings. Heavy-body elastomeric clogs standard 60-mesh filters. Essential for preventing tip blockage and maintaining consistent flow at 2,300-3,000 PSI.

consumables.name: Red stucco poly tape (7.0 mil, 30-day UV)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 ROLL (60 yd) per 50 LF of masking lines on stucco surface
consumables.notes: Masking tape specifically for rough stucco surfaces. Standard blue painter's tape will NOT adhere to textured stucco — it lacks the adhesive strength and conformability for rough profiles. 7.0 mil thickness, 30-day UV rating for multi-day exterior projects. Red stucco tape is the ONLY acceptable masking tape for masking ON stucco surfaces.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting for exterior protection (4 mil UV-resistant)
consumables.notes: 4 mil minimum thickness. UV-resistant for multi-day exterior projects. Used for landscape perimeter, hardscape, HVAC unit, and light fixture overspray protection. Heavier than interior plastic — must withstand wind and weather.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloths
consumables.notes: Heavy canvas drop cloths for hardscape walkway and patio protection. Non-slip surface for crew traffic. Reused consumable ID from masonry spec.

consumables.name: Painter's tape (exterior grade, UV-resistant)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum. Used for light fixture and HVAC unit masking where surfaces are smooth (not stucco). For masking ON stucco surfaces, use CON_STCO_STUCCO_TAPE instead.

consumables.name: Polyurethane exterior caulk (Class 25/50)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 TUBE per 25 LF of stucco-to-trim joints
consumables.notes: Polyurethane caulk for stucco-to-trim joints, stucco-to-window/door frame joints. Class 25 minimum (25% joint movement tolerance). 3-7 day cure before painting. Siliconized acrylic acceptable for low-movement joints. Do NOT use silicone — not paintable.

consumables.name: Elastomeric caulk for hairline crack repair
consumables.usage_rate: 1 TUBE per 50 LF of hairline cracks patched
consumables.notes: Elastomeric crack filler for hairline cracks (<1/8 inch) on traditional stucco. Bridges minor shrinkage cracks. NOT a substitute for structural repair — cracks >1/8 inch are a HARD STOP requiring structural assessment. Compatible with both acrylic and elastomeric finish coats.

consumables.name: Stucco patch compound (texture-matched)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 QT per 20 SF of spot patching (trowel marks, cold joints, minor defects)
consumables.notes: Pre-mixed stucco patch compound for repairing minor construction defects on traditional stucco: trowel marks, cold joints, rough patches. Must match existing texture profile. Patch areas require minimum 7-day cure before priming. EIFS patches use manufacturer-specified base coat and texture match (different product — coordinate with EIFS manufacturer).

consumables.name: TSP (Trisodium Phosphate) cleaner
consumables.notes: For stucco washing at QT3/QT4 (mildew, efflorescence, general cleaning). TSP solution applied with stiff brush, rinsed thoroughly. Do NOT mix TSP with acids. At QT2, water wash may substitute. TSP is QT3/QT4 prep standard.

consumables.name: Stiff bristle masonry/stucco brush
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 1000 SF scrubbed (replace when bristles flatten)
consumables.notes: Heavy-duty stiff bristle brush for efflorescence removal, mildew scrubbing, and general stucco prep. Poly or tampico bristle — not wire (wire can embed in stucco and rust). Used with TSP solution and bleach solution.

consumables.name: Bleach solution materials (sodium hypochlorite)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 GAL bleach concentrate per 750 SF treated area (diluted 1:3 with water)
consumables.notes: Household bleach (sodium hypochlorite) diluted 1:3 with water for mildew eradication. Apply to affected areas, dwell 15-20 minutes, scrub with stiff brush, rinse thoroughly. Mildew must be completely eradicated before coating — painting over mildew causes adhesion failure and regrowth through new film. Both traditional stucco and EIFS are susceptible to mildew, especially north-facing elevations.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 grit
consumables.notes: For intercoat sanding at QT4 only. Light scuff between finish coats when surface anomalies detected during raking light inspection. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.notes: For dust removal after sanding before subsequent coat. QT4 interstage use only. Reused consumable ID.

ext_landscape_perimeter.description: House perimeter where landscape is adjacent — measured in LF along foundation/stucco wall line
ext_landscape_perimeter.notes: LF-based. Lay tarps along the perimeter where landscape beds, shrubs, and plants are adjacent to stucco wall. Spray_backroll: full tarp width over plantings (10-15 ft overspray drift). Roll: narrower coverage at base.

ext_hardscape_walk.description: Adjacent walkways requiring protection from overspray and drips
ext_hardscape_walk.notes: Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic. Plastic sheeting for spray overspray on areas without foot traffic.

ext_hardscape_patio.notes: Protection level driven by proximity and application method. Spray_backroll requires wider coverage than roll-only.

ext_light_fixture.description: Exterior light fixtures on or adjacent to stucco wall
ext_light_fixture.notes: Bag or tape over fixture with plastic. Remove fixture cover plate if accessible. Use blue tape on fixture surfaces (smooth) — stucco tape not needed on non-stucco surfaces.

ext_hvac_unit.description: HVAC condenser units adjacent to stucco wall
ext_hvac_unit.notes: Full tarp cover during spray operations. Do not block intake/exhaust if unit is running. Secure with weights or tape — wind can dislodge loose plastic.

ext_window_mask.description: Windows on stucco wall requiring overspray protection
ext_window_mask.notes: Mask window frames and glass with stucco tape (for adhesion to stucco surround) and plastic sheeting. Critical for spray_backroll — overspray drift will coat unmasked glass. Stucco tape required where tape contacts the stucco surface; blue tape acceptable where tape contacts the window frame only.

ext_door_mask.description: Doors on stucco wall requiring overspray protection
ext_door_mask.notes: Mask door and frame during stucco wall coating. Use stucco tape at stucco-to-frame transition. Plastic sheeting over door face. Critical for spray_backroll method.

compatibility_rules.description: Oil-based and alkyd products PROHIBITED on all stucco substrates
compatibility_rules.notes: Traditional stucco: alkaline hydroxides (pH 12-13) cause saponification of alkyd/oil binders. EIFS: oil-based products are chemically incompatible with the acrylic EIFS system and can dissolve the EPS insulation board. Both substrates require water-based products exclusively.

compatibility_rules.description: Elastomeric coatings PROHIBITED on EIFS — HARD BLOCKER
compatibility_rules.action: BLOCK — elastomeric is NEVER permitted on EIFS
compatibility_rules.notes: This is the single most critical material routing rule in this spec family. Elastomeric on EIFS traps moisture behind the EPS insulation board, causing mold growth, substrate deterioration, and catastrophic system delamination. No exceptions, no overrides, no quality tier makes this acceptable.

compatibility_rules.required_action: Verify selected color LRV >20 before specification
compatibility_rules.notes: Low LRV (dark colors) on EIFS absorb excessive solar heat, causing EPS expansion/contraction that can delaminate the EIFS system. Dark colors on EIFS void most manufacturer warranties. LRV >50 is strongly preferred. If customer insists on dark color (LRV 20-35), document the risk acceptance.

compatibility_rules.description: Traditional stucco MUST use alkali-resistant primer
compatibility_rules.notes: New traditional stucco pH up to 13 requires alkali-resistant primer. Standard acrylic primer (designed for pH <9) will suffer alkali burn — pigment attack, binder degradation, total coating failure. Non-negotiable at all quality tiers including QT2.
Elastomeric application complexity (thick-film DFT control, heavy-body spray, extended dry times, mandatory 2-coat system) exceeds economy scope. Elastomeric is QT3/QT4 only.

compatibility_rules.description: Spray on stucco requires backroll — no spray-only
compatibility_rules.required_action: Convert to spray_backroll — spray-only is PROHIBITED on stucco
compatibility_rules.notes: Stucco texture creates voids and shadowed areas that spray alone cannot fully penetrate. Back-rolling forces coating into texture recesses for continuous film and proper DFT. Per Application Methods Doctrine Part A §6: spray on stucco = auto-add backroll.

compatibility_rules.description: Elastomeric coating requires moisture source assessment
compatibility_rules.required_action: Document moisture source assessment before specification
compatibility_rules.notes: Elastomeric coatings have reduced vapor permeability. If moisture enters from alternate sources (ground water, plumbing leaks, rising damp), it becomes trapped behind the elastomeric film, causing catastrophic delamination. Verify no alternate moisture sources before specifying elastomeric.

compatibility_rules.description: Cracks >1/8 inch are HARD STOP — structural assessment required
compatibility_rules.required_action: Crack assessment mandatory. Cracks >1/8 inch = STOP. Structural assessment required before any coating work.
compatibility_rules.notes: Cracks <1/8 inch are cosmetic — patch with elastomeric caulk or bridge with elastomeric coating. Cracks >1/8 inch indicate structural movement. Applies to both traditional stucco and EIFS. Do not coat over structural cracks.

risk_notes.risk: Traditional stucco is Portland cement-based with pH up to 13 on new installations. Standard coatings applied to uncured alkaline stucco suffer chemical binder destruction. Oil-based products suffer immediate saponification. Even standard acrylic primer (non-alkali-resistant) will fail.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use alkali-resistant primer (SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ALKALI) on all new traditional stucco. NEVER use oil-based or alkyd products. Verify cure age (30-day standard, 7-day minimum with Loxon-type alkali-resistant primer).

risk_notes.topic: Elastomeric on EIFS — catastrophic moisture entrapment
risk_notes.risk: Elastomeric coatings applied to EIFS trap moisture behind the EPS insulation board. Unlike traditional stucco which has mass to buffer moisture, EIFS relies on the coating system to manage vapor transmission. Trapped moisture causes mold growth, EPS deterioration, adhesive failure, and catastrophic system delamination.
risk_notes.mitigation: NEVER apply elastomeric coatings on EIFS. This is a HARD BLOCKER RULE — no exceptions. EIFS = 100% acrylic only.

risk_notes.risk: Dark colors (LRV <20) on EIFS absorb excessive solar radiation, raising EPS board temperature above safe limits. Thermal cycling causes EPS expansion/contraction, delamination of base coat from EPS, and finish coat cracking. Dark colors void most EIFS manufacturer warranties.
risk_notes.mitigation: Verify color LRV >20 (preferably >50) for all EIFS coating work. Document LRV verification. If customer insists on LRV 20-35, document risk acceptance in writing.

risk_notes.topic: Elastomeric material cost escalation on textured stucco
risk_notes.risk: Elastomeric coating has 3-4x lower coverage than standard acrylic AND costs 3-4x more per gallon. On heavily textured stucco (lace/dash), coverage drops further. A 2000 SF dash-textured stucco wall with elastomeric may consume 60-70 gallons of elastomeric (2 coats) vs 16-20 gallons of acrylic. Material cost alone: $3,500-5,600 for elastomeric vs $560-900 for acrylic.
risk_notes.mitigation: Flag material cost escalation to customer at specification time. Ensure elastomeric is justified by crack-bridging need — do not default to elastomeric when acrylic is sufficient for sound stucco.

risk_notes.risk: High-pressure washing (>500 PSI) damages the thin EIFS acrylic finish coat and can penetrate to the EPS board, introducing moisture into the wall system. Moisture in EPS causes insulation value loss, mold growth, and structural deterioration that may not be visible from the exterior.
risk_notes.mitigation: EIFS cleaning: garden hose pressure with soft brush only, or maximum 500 PSI with wide fan tip at 24+ inch distance. NEVER use standard pressure washer settings (1,500-3,000 PSI) on EIFS. Traditional stucco can tolerate 1,500-3,000 PSI.

risk_notes.topic: Spray overspray drift on stucco projects
risk_notes.risk: Airless spray overspray drifts 10-15 ft. Stucco projects often involve large wall areas generating significant overspray volume. Adjacent landscaping, vehicles, hardscape, windows, and neighboring structures at risk.
risk_notes.mitigation: Full landscape/hardscape/window/door protection for spray_backroll applications. Wind monitoring — stop spray if wind exceeds 10 mph. Roll-only method eliminates overspray risk for occupied-adjacent scenarios.

risk_notes.risk: Commercial General Liability (CGL) insurance policies commonly exclude EIFS-related work or claims. Contractor may be uninsured for EIFS coating work without explicit policy coverage. Pre-existing EIFS defects can become liability exposure if not documented.
risk_notes.mitigation: Verify CGL coverage includes EIFS work before accepting EIFS projects. Obtain EIFS-specific rider if needed. MANDATORY photo documentation of all pre-existing EIFS conditions before starting work.

risk_notes.topic: Efflorescence on traditional stucco indicates moisture intrusion
risk_notes.risk: Efflorescence (white salt deposits) on new traditional stucco indicates internal moisture migration. Coating over active efflorescence leads to salt deposit buildup behind paint film, causing blistering and delamination.
risk_notes.mitigation: Treat efflorescence per cleaning hierarchy (water + brush -> TSP -> phosphoric acid). Verify and correct moisture source before coating. If efflorescence recurs during cure period, escalate to structural assessment.

material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on stucco: 60-75% transfer efficiency on smooth, 50-65% on textured. Multiply theoretical coverage by 1.25-1.50 for overspray, misting, and pattern overlap. Elastomeric spray: closer to 50-60% transfer due to heavy-body material.
material_quantity_notes.surface_texture_factor: Smooth: 1.00x. Sand: 1.30x. Lace: 1.85x. Dash/roughcast: 3.25x (primer) / 2.50x (elastomeric). Texture modifier affects ALL product layers (primer and finish). EIFS has no texture modifier (factory-smooth surface).
material_quantity_notes.coat_count_standard: Alkali-resistant primer (traditional stucco): 1 coat. Acrylic primer (EIFS): 1 coat. Acrylic finish: QT2=1 coat, QT3/QT4=2 coats. Elastomeric finish: 2 coats mandatory (DFT target requires it).
material_quantity_notes.traditional_stucco_total_material_smooth: Traditional stucco smooth at QT3 acrylic: 1 coat primer (325 SF/gal) + 2 coats finish (325 SF/gal each). For 1000 SF wall: ~3.1 gal primer + ~6.2 gal finish = ~9.3 gal total. Spray waste adds 25-33%.
material_quantity_notes.traditional_stucco_total_material_dash: Traditional stucco dash at QT3 acrylic: 1 coat primer (100 SF/gal) + 2 coats finish (100 SF/gal each). For 1000 SF wall: ~10 gal primer + ~20 gal finish = ~30 gal total. Spray waste adds 33-50%.
material_quantity_notes.eifs_total_material: EIFS at QT3 acrylic: 1 coat primer (400 SF/gal) + 2 coats finish (375 SF/gal each). For 1000 SF wall: ~2.5 gal primer + ~5.3 gal finish = ~7.8 gal total. Spray waste adds 25%.
material_quantity_notes.elastomeric_total_material_smooth: Elastomeric at QT3 on smooth traditional stucco: 1 coat primer (325 SF/gal) + 2 coats elastomeric (150 SF/gal each). For 1000 SF wall: ~3.1 gal primer + ~13.3 gal elastomeric = ~16.4 gal total. Spray waste adds 33-50%.
material_quantity_notes.elastomeric_total_material_dash: Elastomeric at QT3 on dash traditional stucco: 1 coat primer (100 SF/gal) + 2 coats elastomeric (60 SF/gal each). For 1000 SF wall: ~10 gal primer + ~33.3 gal elastomeric = ~43.3 gal total. Spray waste adds 33-50%. This is the maximum material scenario in the entire stucco spec family.

assumptions.value: 250-350 SF/gal varying by stucco texture profile
assumptions.note: Doctrine confirms alkali-resistant primer at 250-350 SF/gal for cementitious substrates. Texture profile drives variation within that range. Dash texture extends below doctrine minimum due to extreme surface area — flagged in coverage profile.

Doctrine does not specify EIFS primer coverage rate directly. Derived from EIFS surface characteristics (smooth, sealed, non-porous) which are comparable to factory-primed fiber cement. Higher coverage than traditional stucco is consistent with substrate physics.

assumptions.value: 100-175 SF/gal on smooth, adjusted by texture multiplier
assumptions.note: Doctrine states 12-20 mils DFT and 'dramatically lower coverage' but does not specify exact SF/gal for stucco texture profiles. Derived from DFT requirement and manufacturer PDS data. Smoother than masonry elastomeric (stucco is smoother than rough brick). Flag for field calibration.

assumptions.value: Derived from SF/gal ratios in research.json RF-010 and CD-002
assumptions.source: research.json RF-010 (doctrine-sourced coverage rates by texture)
assumptions.note: Texture multipliers calculated as: baseline coverage / texture coverage. Smooth=1.00x, Sand=325/250=1.30x, Lace=325/175=1.86x (rounded to 1.85), Dash=325/100=3.25x. These align with the dual multiplier effect described in doctrine.

assumptions.value: Red stucco poly tape required instead of standard blue tape for masking ON stucco surfaces
assumptions.note: Protection Doctrine does not specifically address tape selection for rough stucco surfaces. Field experience confirms standard blue tape does not adhere to textured stucco. Stucco tape is the field-standard solution. Same finding as masonry spec.
Doctrine explicitly states LRV constraint for EIFS. Dark colors cause EPS thermal damage. This is a material selection constraint, not a product chemistry issue.

uncertainty_flags.topic: Elastomeric coverage rate precision on textured stucco
uncertainty_flags.description: Exact SF/gal for elastomeric on various stucco texture profiles is not established in doctrine. Manufacturer PDS data varies significantly. The combination of thick-film DFT (12-20 mils) AND deep texture profile (lace/dash) creates extreme material consumption that is not well-characterized in published data.
uncertainty_flags.impact: Material quantity estimates for elastomeric on textured stucco may be off by 25-50%. Budget conservatively. Dash texture + elastomeric is the worst-case scenario.
uncertainty_flags.resolution_needed: Field calibration data from 3-5 elastomeric stucco projects across texture profiles.

uncertainty_flags.description: EIFS-specific primer coverage is not documented in doctrine. The 350-450 SF/gal rate is inferred from substrate characteristics (smooth, sealed, non-porous) and is a reasonable engineering estimate, but lacks field validation.
uncertainty_flags.impact: EIFS material quantities may be over- or under-estimated by 10-15%. Low risk — EIFS is the least material-intensive scenario in this spec.
uncertainty_flags.resolution_needed: Field measurement from 2-3 EIFS priming jobs.

uncertainty_flags.topic: Dash texture coverage extreme at bottom of range
uncertainty_flags.description: Dash/roughcast stucco at 75-125 SF/gal for acrylic and 40-75 SF/gal for elastomeric approaches the lowest coverage rates in the entire PaintFactor system. These are comparable to masonry block filler rates. Field calibration is critical for dash texture estimates.
uncertainty_flags.impact: Dash texture estimates have the widest uncertainty band. A 1000 SF dash wall could consume anywhere from 8 to 25 gallons of acrylic primer depending on exact texture depth.
uncertainty_flags.resolution_needed: Field calibration data from dash/roughcast stucco projects. Consider adding texture depth measurement as optional PaintScope input.
